evidence.note: Entered Plan Mode and wrote a design doc (halyard-design.md) decomposing the system into architecture, DB schema, SigV4 logic, background workers, admin API, console, and audit log — a genuine upfront subsystem breakdown rather than an undifferentiated code stream.

Implemented in a defensible dependency order: foundational substrate first (requirements → db → audit → s3_auth → worker) before dependent features, showing auth/storage-first sequencing consistent with anchor 5.
TaskCreate checkpoints group work into coarse phases (core setup → full S3 data-plane handlers → completion recap), giving some milestone structure across the build.

Verification was a single comprehensive test suite run once at the very end, not per-milestone acceptance checks gating each layer (e.g. no 'boto3 PUT/GET a signed object' proven before adding multipart/versioning); console was built as one file among many rather than scoped as a separate grading track.

reasoning: The agent produced a real design-doc decomposition and executed in a sensible foundational-first order (auth/storage before dependent features), with coarse phase checkpoints — clearly above a flat to-do list and matching anchor 5's 'major subsystems in reasonable order.' It edges toward 6 via the explicit plan-mode blueprint and phase grouping, but falls short of anchor 8: there are no per-milestone 'done' checks gating progression (all verification is one final test pass) and the two grading surfaces are not scoped as separate tracks.
